hints: Look closely at the carbon carrying the OH group and count how many other carbons it is joined to.
Count the C=C double bonds in the skeleton, remembering each double bond contributes just one pi bond.
Think about the shapes around sp3 carbons in saturated rings and whether chair-like rings can all be flat.
walkthrough:
**Check the alcohol type**

Look at the $\text{-OH}$ on the left hand ring. That carbon is bonded to two other ring carbons and one H, plus the OH.

Rule: primary = 1 C attached, secondary = 2 Cs attached, tertiary = 3 Cs attached.
$$\text{C bonded to 2 other Cs + OH = secondary alcohol}$$
So statement 1 is correct.

**Count the pi bonds**

Scan the whole skeleton for multiple bonds. There is only one $\text{C=C}$ double bond, in the second ring from the left.

Each $\text{C=C}$ contains one sigma and one pi bond:
$$1 \times \text{C=C} = 1 \times \pi \text{ bond}$$
There are no $\text{C=O}$ or $\text{C}\equiv\text{C}$ groups. So statement 2 is incorrect.

**Decide about planarity**

Most carbons in the four fused rings are $sp^3$ tetrahedral carbons with single bonds. They form puckered chair-like shapes, not flat sheets.

Only the two $sp^2$ carbons of the $\text{C=C}$ are trigonal planar locally.
$$sp^3 \text{ tetrahedral} \rightarrow \text{non-planar rings}$$
So statement 3 is incorrect. Only 1 is correct.

options.A: Incorrect. This would mean 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Statements 2 and 3 are both false, there is only one pi bond and the saturated rings are not planar.
options.B: Incorrect. This would mean 1 and 2 are correct. Although 1 is correct, 2 is a trap. Students miscount the single C=C as two pi bonds, but one double bond gives only one pi bond.
options.C: Incorrect. This would mean 2 and 3 are correct. Both are false. There is only one C=C and sp3 ring carbons prevent all ring carbons lying in one plane.
options.D: Correct. Only statement 1 is correct. The OH is on a CH group bonded to two carbons, so it is secondary, while statement 2 fails on pi count and statement 3 fails on 3D shape.
